code.originalText: Three-month heart failure and blood pressure review

text.paragraph: Three-month heart failure and blood pressure review. [S]

Mr. Roosevelt returns for his three-month review. He propels his wheelchair on level ground without stopping and is breathless only on long ramps. He sleeps on one pillow and has had no leg swelling for several weeks. His home weights have held at 83 to 84 kg for a month, and his home blood pressures run in the 120s over 70s. He felt more energetic within a few weeks of the iron infusions and is working full days again. He has had no lightheadedness on transfers, no breast tenderness on spironolactone, and no muscle aches on atorvastatin. He has not smoked since April, cravings are now rare, and he asks to stop the patch. [S]

value.displayName: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure

list.item:
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, euvolemic (I50.22). No congestion on examination and a stable weight; NYHA class II. NT-proBNP has fallen from 2850 to 980 pg/mL and the KCCQ-12 has risen from 38 to 64, meeting his goal. Potassium 4.6 mmol/L and creatinine 1.24 mg/dL (eGFR 66) on sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg and spironolactone. [S]
Increase carvedilol to 12.5 mg twice daily with food; heart rate 70 and blood pressure 128/78 allow it.
Stop daily furosemide, since he is euvolemic with a stable weight; call for a weight gain of more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week, or for returning leg swelling.
Keep sacubitril/valsartan at 49/51 mg for now, to make one change at a time while carvedilol rises and furosemide stops; reconsider at the six-month review.
Continue spironolactone and empagliflozin.
Basic metabolic panel in one to two weeks, because potassium can rise once the loop diuretic stops.
Referral to cardiac rehabilitation with seated, upper-body exercise training.
Repeat echocardiogram at the six-month review.

Iron deficiency in heart failure, repleted (D50.9). Hemoglobin 13.6 g/dL, ferritin 236 ng/mL, and transferrin saturation 27 percent after two intravenous iron doses: repleted, and the anemia has resolved. [S]
No further iron now; iron studies yearly.

Hypertensive heart disease (I11.0). Blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, below the 130/80 target, with home readings in the 120s over 70s. [S]
Keep it below target through the six-month review.

Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, in early remission (F17.210). Abstinent since April, meeting his goal, after a 13-week nicotine patch course. [S]
Stop the patch.
Relapse plan: restart a patch with a short-acting nicotine product at once if he smokes again.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). Atorvastatin 40 mg taken every day without muscle symptoms. The confirming lipid panel has not been drawn. [S]
Lipid panel with the six-month laboratory tests.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022); 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, heart failure and hypertension monographs (2026); Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions (2021); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026)

Follow-up: Basic metabolic panel in one to two weeks after stopping furosemide. Six-month heart failure review with an echocardiogram, laboratory tests including a lipid panel, and the KCCQ-12. Next scheduled visit 1944-09-25: six-month heart failure review with repeat echocardiogram. [S]
